title: Northbridge Pay partnership scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Account: Northbridge Pay (mid-stage fintech; raised Series B 2024). Building a real-time risk/decisioning layer for payments and merchant onboarding. Heavy on PII, regulatory constraints in EU + UK.
- Why target: need low-latency model inference near data, interest in private deployments + dedicated capacity. Potential for Dedicated contract + Private deployment for higher tiers.

Quick notes from public research:
- HQ: London; engineering hub in Porto.
- Tech stack: Python, Kafka, Kubernetes, Postgres, Redis. Mentions of "on-prem for EU customers" in recent blog post.
- Hiring: multiple ML infra and security roles in last 6 months -> likely scaling infra.
- Public benchmarks: touts 30ms decisioning for fraud rules today (rule-based + classifier), looking to add LLM-assisted verification and intent classification.

Key stakeholders (inferred / to verify):
- CTO: Maya Alvarez (strategic, cares about vendor SLAs and ops burden)
- Head of ML: Jonah Park (wants model parity and reproducibility)
- Head of Security/Compliance: Pieter van Dijk (GDPR + SOC2)
- Product lead (fraud): Rina Choudhury (owns decisioning roadmap)

Initial value props to surface:
- Predictable latency: Redwood Dedicated pools to meet p95 latency SLOs for decisioning pipelines (can demo 5–50ms ranges depending on model).
- Private deployment option: VPC + on-prem package for EU-regulated customers (no data plane egress).
- Cost control levers: batching, KV/prefix caching for typical request patterns (short sequences, lots of repeated prefixes in verification flows).
- Observability: per-route token-level cost + rollout tools to compare model quality against current classifiers.

Suggested outreach sequence (3-touch):
1) Cold email (Day 0) — short, hyper-personalized
   Subject: Demo: low-latency model inference for EU payments decisioning
   Body: 2–3 lines: reference blog post about on-prem + quick value: "We help teams cut model inference costs and keep p95 latency under X ms with a private deployment pattern for regulated EU flows. Quick 20-min demo next week?"

2) LinkedIn connect + message (Day 3) — note on mutual goal: safer EU product rollout, offer a one-pager and benchmark sample.

3) Follow-up email + ask for a technical contact (Day 7) — attach short architecture diagram and suggested POC footprint.

Cold email draft (longer):
Hi Maya,

Saw Northbridge Pay's note about enabling on-prem capabilities for EU customers — impressive roadmap. We helped a payments company move ML decisioning (high-cardinality rules + LLM enrichment) to a hybrid model that met their GDPR constraints while cutting per-decision cost by ~30%.

If you're lining up an evaluation, would love to run a short benchmark against a 90–95th-percentile latency target and share concrete tuning knobs (quantization, KV caching) that kept throughput predictable. 20 min call to align?

Best,
Anika

Voicemail script (for CTO):
"Maya — Anika from Redwood Inference. Quick note: we’ve got a pattern that helps payments teams run decisioning models with private deployments in EU regions while keeping p95 latency predictable. Left an email with a proposed 20-min time. Thanks."

Discovery questions (for first technical call):
- What does a typical decisioning request look like (tokens, structure)?
- Current p50/p95 latency targets and observed p95 under load?
- QPS and peak concurrency (daily & seasonal peaks)?
- Are you using any transformer-based models today in decision path? Which families/versions?
- Data residency requirements (EU-only, do you accept US control plane?)
- Who will be the technical champion/internal owner for a POC?
- How do you currently validate model quality/regressions?

Objection handling (common):
- "We already host models internally." -> Acknowledge: great. Differentiate: Redwood reduces ops overhead for scaling, provides traffic-split rollouts, and fallback to smaller model variants automatically to protect latency SLAs. Offer a benchmark showing control-plane overhead vs DIY.
- "Cost — we can do it cheaper ourselves." -> Show unit economics: include per-100k-request cost with/without caching + expected savings from batching + cheaper quantized variants. Offer a short TCO sheet.
- "Security/compliance concerns." -> Point to Private + on-prem packaging, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2 evidence; propose an NDA + security questionnaire early.
- "Vendor lock-in." -> Emphasize deployment abstraction + ability to pin model versions and export artifacts; talk about hybrid model where we operate the control plane and customers can self-host the runtimes.

POC scoping (lightweight first POC):
- Goal: show parity on decisioning accuracy and hit p95 <= 3x current baseline (or target provided by NB).
- Data: use synthetic or redacted sample payloads if NB won’t share raw PII.
- Bench: 1 endpoint, two model variants (fast smaller quantized vs full), 72-hour steady-state + short spike test.
- Success criteria: p95 latency target met, model output parity within defined tolerance, no data egress to non-EU region.

Internal asks (what I need from our side):
- Engineering: quick benchmark config for 2 GPUs (A100x2 or equivalent) to estimate Dedicated pricing. (Tag: @Liam Chen)
- Security: KMS/HSM notes + any additional EU compliance artifacts to send to them. (@Sofia Martinez)
- Sales: standard Private deployment T&Cs and a one-pager for EU market. (CC: growth-sales)

Notes on pricing posture for outreach:
- Lead with Dedicated as a predictable baseline. Mention Private deployment as the main gating capability for enterprise EU accounts.
- Prepare cadence for Reserved capacity options (monthly commits) vs usage-based.

Possible red flags to watch for:
- Very low QPS but high compliance needs (might be a small revenue opportunity but high SOW).
- Reluctance to provide any sample payloads — could stall technical validation.
- Stakeholders distributed with no clear technical owner -> need to push for an ML infra contact.

Next steps:
- Send Day 0 cold email to CTO + CC Head of ML.
- If no reply by Day 4, LinkedIn + attach 1-pager + one-sentence benchmark claim.
- Build a tailored TCO slide and a short one-page POC runbook to attach on first technical ask.

Quick scratch ideas for one-pager headings:
- "Why inference matters for payments decisioning"
- "Redwood deployment patterns for regulated EU customers"
- "Cost and latency tradeoffs: sample numbers"
- "POC runbook (72 hours)"

Random: check CONFLUENCE-REDWOOD-PRD-789 for recent EU compliance collateral before sending.

-- end scratchpad --
